project.title: [Client] Sales Cloud
project.description: What we learned in discovery, what we will build together, and the path to go-live. This is the full written version of the readout presentation.

paragraphs: [Client] sells to mid-market manufacturers through a team of eight reps and two sales managers, with about 2,400 leads a year coming in from the website.

Today every website form arrives as an email that someone copies into Salesforce by hand. About a third never make it in, assignment waits for a weekly meeting, and nothing tells a manager a lead has gone cold until the month-end report.
This project sets up Sales Cloud so that every lead is captured, owned and followed up from the moment it arrives, and converts into an account, contact and opportunity without retyping.

pillars.d: Website forms create leads directly, one per person, with the page they came from.
Leads are assigned by territory the moment they are created, and untouched leads are flagged after two business days.

pillars.t: One step from lead to opportunity
pillars.d: Qualifying a lead creates the account, contact and opportunity, matched to existing accounts first.

figure.caption: The system at a glance. Leads arrive from the website, live in Sales Cloud, and leave as opportunities and reports.

s05.lede: The launch includes everything [Client] needs to capture, assign and convert leads on day one.

rows.build: The contact and demo request forms create one lead each, matched on email before a new one is created, with the form page recorded.
rows.solves: Ends copying form emails by hand and the leads lost on the way.

rows.build: Leads in the United States go to the rep who owns the state; others go to the international queue.
A lead with no activity in two business days is flagged to the sales manager.
rows.solves: Managers see cold leads in days, not at month end.

rows.build: Qualifying a lead creates the contact, account and opportunity from its fields; the opportunity opens at Discovery with a close date 60 days out.
Conversion looks for an existing account by website domain, then by name, before creating one.
Leads by source and territory, time to first touch, and conversion by rep.
rows.solves: Managers see the funnel without exports.

s06.lede: The build is sequenced so each layer rests on the one before it.

layers.d: Users, roles and territories, so every record has an owner and a team.
Lead fields, statuses and the closed reasons list, with the web forms connected.
Territory assignment, the untouched flag and one-step conversion with account matching.
Dashboards for managers and reps, built on the data the first three layers produce.

s08.lede: The workflows follow the way the work runs. Each one was played back in discovery and updated with [Client]'s corrections.

W-01.today: Form emails are copied into Salesforce by hand when someone gets to them, and leads wait for the weekly meeting to be assigned.
W-01.changes: Each form creates a lead on its own and it is assigned by territory the moment it lands.

W-02.today: Reps create the account, contact and opportunity by hand, sometimes duplicating an account that exists.
W-02.changes: Qualifying the lead creates all three in one step, matched to an existing account first.

journeys.outcome: From form to opportunity in one day, with nothing retyped and no duplicate account.

s11.intro: Most of what we heard sits inside the agreed scope. A few points differ from the SOW, and we list them here so everyone works from the same picture.

s11.principle: If [Client] needs it to capture, assign and convert leads on day one, it is in this project. Anything beyond that is set aside for a future phase unless it is explicitly pulled into scope.

s12.lede: How [Client] and Kicksaw will know the project succeeded.

rows.how: Every contact and demo request form submission is in Salesforce, with no manual entry.
Every new lead has an owner within minutes of arriving.
Managers act on untouched leads within the week instead of at month end.
Conversions happen in one step, and new duplicate accounts stop appearing.

rows.why: Too loose a match merges different companies.
